The main gaps are origin-linked monitoring of maize grain outside Europe and the Western Pacific, inorganic arsenic in maize, and any study that measures the same corn before and after cleaning, milling or cooking.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Two records about Health Canada diaper-rash monographs matched the search but have no readable file; they are unrelated to corn.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Corn FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-corn" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-corn" data-question="What heavy metals are found in corn?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in corn?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury are measured most often, and in monitored maize grain and sweet corn most results are below reporting limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Field studies also report nickel and chromium, which reached about 1,400–1,900 µg/kg in dried maize from Bangladesh fields.<sup class="cite">[[sources/islam2014-bangladesh-cereals-pulses-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Islam MS, Ahmed MK, Habibullah-Al-Mamun M · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/islam2014-bangladesh-cereals-pulses-metals">Heavy Metals in Cereals and Pulses: Health Implications in Bangladesh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/islam2014-bangladesh-cereals-pulses-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-corn" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-corn" data-question="How do heavy metals get into corn?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into corn?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Corn takes up cadmium and nickel from soil, and lead and mercury also reach it from dust and emissions settling on the plant.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil contaminate corn in the vicinity of a cement-manufacturing plant: potential health implications</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Exposure Science &amp; Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/gu2019-maize-peanut-heavy-metals-guangxi|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gu Q, Yu T, Yang Z, Ji J, Hou Q, Wang L, Wei X, Zhang Q · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gu2019-maize-peanut-heavy-metals-guangxi">Prediction and risk assessment of five heavy metals in maize and peanut: a case study of Guangxi, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Toxicology and Pharmacology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gu2019-maize-peanut-heavy-metals-guangxi">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Wastewater irrigation and mining or industrial land raised lead, cadmium, mercury or arsenic in the studies available.<sup class="cite">[[sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adel S. El-Hassanin, Magdy R. Samak, Gomaa N. Abdel-Rahman, Yahia H. Abu-Sree, Essam M. Saleh · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Risk assessment of human exposure to lead and cadmium in maize grains cultivated in soils irrigated either with low-quality water or freshwater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 7:10-15</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Romero-Crespo P, Jiménez-Oyola S, Salgado-Almeida B, Zambrano-Anchundia J, Goyburo-Chávez C, González-Valoys A, Higueras P · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Trace elements in farmland soils and crops, and probabilistic health risk assessment in areas influenced by mining activity in Ecuador</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Geochemistry and Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/romero-crespo2023-trace-elements-crops-ecuador-mining">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bai2022-arsenic-coal-burning-shaanxi|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bai AM, Li Q, Li Y, Fan ZX, Li XQ, Tan WH, Cao DY, Kang YJ · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bai2022-arsenic-coal-burning-shaanxi">Investigation Into Environmental Selenium and Arsenic Levels and Arseniasis Prevalence in an Arsenic-Affected Coal-Burning Area</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bai2022-arsenic-coal-burning-shaanxi">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-corn-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-corn-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of corn have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of corn have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, sweet corn measured lowest per kilogram: cooked US sweet corn was below 4 µg/kg in all 27 composites and raw sweet corn medians were below 1.4–10 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Maize grain had a European median below 20 µg/kg, and the higher figure largely reflects that grain is dry.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-or-regions-produce-corn-with-the-lowest-lead" data-anchor="which-countries-or-regions-produce-corn-with-the-lowest-lead" data-question="Which countries or regions produce corn with the lowest lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries or regions produce corn with the lowest lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among reporting regions, European maize grain had the fewest results above the 200 µg/kg cereal limit (8 of 890), against 24 of 327 in Western Pacific submissions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> GEMS/Food does not name the country where corn was grown, so the evidence cannot rank producing countries; growing near industry, wastewater or mines matters more in the field studies.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil contaminate corn in the vicinity of a cement-manufacturing plant: potential health implications</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Exposure Science &amp; Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adel S. El-Hassanin, Magdy R. Samak, Gomaa N. Abdel-Rahman, Yahia H. Abu-Sree, Essam M. Saleh · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Risk assessment of human exposure to lead and cadmium in maize grains cultivated in soils irrigated either with low-quality water or freshwater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 7:10-15</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-foods-made-from-corn-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-foods-made-from-corn-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do foods made from corn also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do foods made from corn also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Corn flour, flakes, popcorn, canned corn and other corn foods are measured separately and have their own pages, so their results are not repeated here.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> One European study found that infant porridges mixing rice with maize and other grains had lower inorganic arsenic than pure rice porridges (median 10 against 66 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/carey2018-rice-dilution-infant-food-eu-arsenic|28]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Carey M, Donaldson E, Signes-Pastor AJ, class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/carey2018-rice-dilution-infant-food-eu-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-corn-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-corn-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in corn mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in corn mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No source in the ledger turned corn concentrations into a verified estimate of population intake, so the evidence cannot say how much corn contributes to lead or cadmium exposure overall. Typical retail sweet corn is low per serving, while maize eaten daily as a staple from contaminated fields is the case where intake could matter.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-corn" data-anchor="can-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-corn" data-question="Can processing reduce heavy metals in corn?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can processing reduce heavy metals in corn?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No study in the library measured the same corn before and after cleaning, husking, milling or cooking, so no reduction can be stated. Drying raises the concentration per kilogram because water is removed, which is why dried-grain results look higher than sweet corn as eaten.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil contaminate corn in the vicinity of a cement-manufacturing plant: potential health implications</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Exposure Science &amp; Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saleem2025-nd-vegetables-hra|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saleem M, Wang Y, Pierce D, Sens DA, Somji S, Garrett SH · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saleem2025-nd-vegetables-hra">Concentration and Potential Non-Carcinogenic and Carcinogenic Health Risk Assessment of Metals in Locally Grown Vegetables</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saleem2025-nd-vegetables-hra">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cooking-corn-get-rid-of-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-cooking-corn-get-rid-of-heavy-metals" data-question="Does cooking corn get rid of heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cooking corn get rid of heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Heat does not destroy metals, and no study measured the same corn before and after cooking. Cooked sweet corn in monitoring had lead and cadmium similar to raw sweet corn from the same regions, mostly below reporting limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-corn-contain-inorganic-arsenic-like-rice" data-anchor="does-corn-contain-inorganic-arsenic-like-rice" data-question="Does corn contain inorganic arsenic like rice?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does corn contain inorganic arsenic like rice?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Much less is known: only 12 maize results were speciated for inorganic arsenic, and 2 were detected, at 8 and 310 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Total arsenic in monitored maize grain had a median below 12–15 µg/kg, but field maize from Bangladesh and arsenic-affected areas of China and Ecuador was far higher.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a MK, Habibullah-Al-Mamun M · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/islam2014-bangladesh-cereals-pulses-metals">Heavy Metals in Cereals and Pulses: Health Implications in Bangladesh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-corn-lower-in-arsenic-and-cadmium-than-rice" data-anchor="is-corn-lower-in-arsenic-and-cadmium-than-rice" data-question="Is corn lower in arsenic and cadmium than rice?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is corn lower in arsenic and cadmium than rice?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the same contaminated areas, maize carried less than rice: about a third of the mercury near Chinese coal-fired power plants and 260 against 460 µg/kg cadmium near Chengdu.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/liu2022-heavy-metals-rice-maize-chengdu|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Liu Q, Li X, He L · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" Chengdu Plain, Sichuan, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/liu2022-heavy-metals-rice-maize-chengdu">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Maize lead was similar to rice in Chengdu (290 against 300 µg/kg), so the advantage is not universal.<sup class="cite">[[sources/liu2022-heavy-metals-rice-maize-chengdu|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Liu Q, Li X, He L · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/liu2022-heavy-metals-rice-maize-chengdu">Health risk assessment of heavy metals in soils and food crops from a coexist area of heavily industrialized and href="../sources/liu2022-heavy-metals-rice-maize-chengdu">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-corn-a-concern-for-babies-and-children" data-anchor="is-corn-a-concern-for-babies-and-children" data-question="Is corn a concern for babies and children?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is corn a concern for babies and children?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Infant cereals and baby foods containing corn are covered on their own pages; on this page, retail sweet corn was low in lead, with every cooked US composite below 4 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Maize from contaminated fields would matter most where it is a daily staple for children, and the evidence has no child-specific exposure estimate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil contaminate corn in the vicinity of a cement-manufacturing plant: potential health implications</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Exposure Science &amp; Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adel S. El-Hassanin, Magdy R. Samak, Gomaa N. Abdel-Rahman, Yahia H. Abu-Sree, Essam M. Saleh · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Risk assessment of human exposure to lead and cadmium in maize grains cultivated in soils irrigated either with low-quality water or freshwater</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 7:10-15</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-sweet-corn-safer-than-field-corn" data-anchor="is-sweet-corn-safer-than-field-corn" data-question="Is sweet corn safer than field corn?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is sweet corn safer than field corn?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Sweet corn had lower lead per kilogram in monitoring, but it is mostly water and is judged against a lower lead limit (100 against 200 µg/kg in the EU).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Both forms grown near industry, wastewater or mines can carry more metal, so where the corn grew matters more than the type.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adel S. <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="has-lead-in-corn-been-falling" data-anchor="has-lead-in-corn-been-falling" data-question="Has lead in corn been falling?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Has lead in corn been falling?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In European maize grain submitted to GEMS/Food, 4 of 233 results from 2001–2007 and 4 of 257 from 2008–2013 exceeded 200 µg/kg lead, against none of 400 from 2014–2020.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Coverage changed over the years, so this is a monitoring pattern rather than a fixed panel of farms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-imported-corn-higher-in-metals-than-locally-grown-corn" data-anchor="is-imported-corn-higher-in-metals-than-locally-grown-corn" data-question="Is imported corn higher in metals than locally grown corn?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is imported corn higher in metals than locally grown corn?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In European submissions, imported maize grain had lead and cadmium similar to domestic grain, and imported sweet corn had lower cadmium (median below 2.4 against 2.6–4 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The export does not name the producing country, so this cannot identify which origins are higher.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-corn-grown-near-mines-or-factories-higher-in-metals" data-anchor="is-corn-grown-near-mines-or-factories-higher-in-metals" data-question="Is corn grown near mines or factories higher in metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is corn grown near mines or factories higher in metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in every such study available: downwind of a cement plant, beside coal-fired power plants, near a battery plant, on wastewater-irrigated fields and in mining areas, corn carried more lead, mercury, cadmium or arsenic than control or market corn.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abatemi-Usman S, Akindele O, Ayanlade A, Perez M, Attahiru I, Norton G, Feldmann J, Krupp E · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Trace elements concentrations in soil contaminate corn in the vicinity of a cement-manufacturing plant: potential health implications</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Exposure Science &amp; Environmental Epidemiology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abatemi-usman2023-corn-cement-nigeria">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/el-hassanin2020-egypt-maize-pb-cd|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adel S. <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-corn-metal-test-is-good-enough" data-anchor="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-corn-metal-test-is-good-enough" data-question="How can I tell whether a corn metal test is good enough?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How can I tell whether a corn metal test is good enough?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Check that the quantification limit sits well below the limit for the form tested, for example below 20 µg/kg cadmium for sweet corn in the EU, and that the result states the form and basis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The FDA reported cooked corn with limits of 4 µg/kg lead, 3 µg/kg arsenic and 1 µg/kg mercury, a useful benchmark for sensitivity.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
